title: KV cache TTL serialization bug leading to cross-tenant stale entries and eviction storms - followup
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Follow-up for the 2025-02-16 incident where a small serialization change to the KV cache metadata caused TTL fields to be written without namespace-scoped versioning, allowing stale entries from one tenant to be read by another in rare race conditions. The result was intermittent cross-tenant stale reads (cache poisoning), elevated eviction churn, and downstream tail-latency spikes for several hosted customers. This ticket consolidates findings, tracks mitigations, and coordinates deliverables (code fixes, tests, dashboards, runbooks, and customer communications).
incident_summary: At ~2025-02-16T22:12 UTC a deploy of kv-metadata-serializer introduced a regression: serialized TTL/version blobs dropped the explicit namespace tag when the metadata blob used the compact form. Combined with a previously latent race in prefix lookups during concurrent writes, host A occasionally read a stale entry originating from host B under a different tenant namespace. That stale entry had an older TTL that still appeared valid, so it bypassed eviction heuristics and consequently forced eviction storms when the true current entry arrived, creating high CPU and memory pressure on inference workers in the affected region.

root_cause: A combination of three factors: 1) a change in kv metadata serialization that omitted namespace/version tag in compact-mode blobs, 2) a previously tolerated race in prefix lookup vs write path that allowed a reader to resolve a stale compact blob before the new entry was fully persisted, and 3) the eviction heuristics assuming TTL was authoritative without verifying namespace integrity. Individually these were low risk; together they produced cross-tenant stale reads and downstream eviction storms.
mitigation: Immediate rollback of the serializer (v2.1.3 -> v2.1.2) stopped new occurrences. Short-term: lowered concurrent write window and enabled stricter verification in the read path (compare namespace tag when present). Long-term: the fix is to change the serializer to always include explicit namespace/version tags even in compact form, strengthen prefix lookup synchronization, and add a defensive read-time namespace verification as a canary during rollout.
